description: I’m interested in space, technology, and creative problem-solving. I’m excited to explore NASA’s open data and turn an idea into a useful project.
summary: Field Shift is a browser-based crop rotation lab that helps agricultural vocational students in Malatya, Türkiye, practise climate adaptation before a mistake costs a real harvest. Students plan wheat, barley, chickpea or lentil across three plots and three seasons, then watch the seasons play out on 8,036 days of NASA POWER daily weather (2003–2025). Rain refills a soil water store, temperature drives FAO-56 Hargreaves evapotranspiration, and crop stage coefficients turn that into daily water demand. A decision report pinpoints the first water deficit and replays single changes on identical weather, so learners see the trade-offs between water use, cereal targets, heat stress and bare-soil days. Season rainfall at this NASA point ranged from 199 mm to 534 mm, so no single plan fits every year: students learn to weigh water, soil and food and reach their own reasoned plan. The prototype runs offline in English and Turkish, with a deterministic, tested model. Model inputs are illustrative and await local validation. Field Shift supports SDGs 4, 2, 6 and 13 by training the people who will make future farm decisions.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

Field Shift is a three-season crop rotation simulator for Malatya, Türkiye. Learners choose wheat, barley, chickpea or lentil for three plots, with early, standard or late sowing, and simulate three seasons on historical NASA POWER weather. Two bundled scenarios work offline: the lowest-rainfall window (Sep 2015–Aug 2018) and a near-median window (Sep 2008–Aug 2011).

HOW IT WORKS

• NASA POWER daily precipitation (PRECTOTCORR) refills modeled soil water storage.

• Mean, maximum and minimum temperature (T2M, T2M_MAX, T2M_MIN) drive FAO-56 Hargreaves reference evapotranspiration.

• Crop stage coefficients (Kc) convert reference ET into daily crop water demand. Soil water is used first, then a limited irrigation budget.

• T2M_MAX is checked against crop heat thresholds during sensitive stages.

• A decision report shows the first water deficit, a monthly deficit map, relative yield (FAO-33), heat exposure, crop-family repetition and uncovered plot-days. It then replays single crop or sowing-date changes on identical weather and ranks feasible alternatives.

• A shared-water mode lets three farms divide one irrigation budget. An optional reflection quiz and session export support classroom use.

BENEFITS AND INTENDED IMPACT

On a real farm a rotation mistake costs a season. Field Shift gives students a safe place to see consequences: when and where water runs out, and how saving water can leave soil bare for longer. Teachers get a ready discussion tool. Our intended impact is better water, soil and food decisions by the next generation of farmers, supporting SDGs 4, 2, 6 and 13. Learning impact has not yet been measured; a classroom pilot is our next step.

WHY IT IS CREATIVE

Replaying identical weather isolates the effect of one decision, which no real farm can offer. NASA data is not a backdrop: it drives every water and heat calculation in the game.

TOOLS

HTML, CSS and JavaScript (ES modules), using only browser and Node.js standard APIs; a standalone single-file build that runs offline. Node test runner for 10 model tests; a browser integration test (keyboard use, reload, replay, 360 px layout, both languages).

FACTORS WE CONSIDERED

Honest limits: soils, crop coefficients, sowing dates and water quotas are illustrative and need local expert validation. Relative yield is a model index, not a harvest forecast. We do not claim tonnes, income or measured water savings. Data provenance is archived with the API request URL and SHA-256 hashes.
